summary: Fourth repair of documented step M4-S05, for F-62 (reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M5.md run 7): after the section 10 fix the deployed process is found and the Case enters it, but the two milestone methods fail on behaviour. Confirmed diagnosis: CaseMilestoneService's CaseMilestone query and Database.update ran WITH USER_MODE / default user mode (apiVersion 67.0), and no permission set in this build (artefacts/M2-S02/) grants any objectPermissions on CaseMilestone at all, so the update was refused for the Tier 1 persona under allOrNone=false and the refusal landed silently in result.failures, which the test never asserted. Unlike the three prior repairs (sections 8-10, test-only), this repair changes shipped code: CaseMilestoneService.cls's CaseMilestone SELECT now carries WITH SYSTEM_MODE and its Database.update carries AccessLevel.SYSTEM_MODE, each with a reason comment, per skills/apex/apex-security-patterns' access-mode table for platform-utility code (chosen over granting the persona Edit on CaseMilestone, which was rejected as the same anti-pattern skills/apex/test-class-standards Gotcha 15 already named). CaseMilestoneServiceTest.cls gained three new Assert.areEqual(0, result.failures.size(), ...) assertions after the three completeMilestones call sites that previously had none, so a refused write now fails loudly.
confidence_rationale: The declared checker, the requested check_test_class_standards.py (both without and with --strict), and check-outputs all exit 0 / ok. Confidence stays at MEDIUM, not HIGH, because: (1) no offline Apex compiler exists (agents/apex-builder/GATES.md Gate D) and this build has no target_org_alias, so this repair -- especially the AccessLevel.SYSTEM_MODE argument to Database.update, a syntax this class had not used before -- is confirmed only by the operator's next dry run (run 8); (2) this is the first repair in this step's history to change shipped code, so the M4/M5 gate evidence built against the unchanged CaseMilestoneService.cls no longer describes the deployed class; and (3) a cross-skill tension (skills/apex/apex-stripinaccessible-and-fls-enforcement's trigger-body line vs. skills/apex/apex-security-patterns' docs-grounded rule) had to be resolved by source-hierarchy judgment rather than by an unambiguous single citation.

findings.title: F-62 diagnosis confirmed exactly: no permission set in this build grants CaseMilestone access
findings.detail: grep -rn CaseMilestone across artefacts/M2-S02/ (re-run this session) returns no objectPermissions hit. Reading Case_Agent_Core.permissionset-meta.xml directly, its five objectPermissions blocks name Case, Account, Contact, EmailMessage, Entitlement -- CaseMilestone is absent, not read-only. At apiVersion 67.0 default user mode, both the CaseMilestone query and the Database.update in CaseMilestoneService.completeMilestones therefore ran as the Tier 1 persona with zero grants on the object, and allOrNone=false meant the refusal landed in result.failures rather than throwing -- exactly the coordinator's reading, confirmed rather than revised.

findings.title: System mode chosen over granting the persona Edit on CaseMilestone, per Gotcha 15's discipline applied one object over
findings.detail: skills/apex/apex-security-patterns' access-mode table names platform-utility code on a 67.0+ class as the WITH SYSTEM_MODE / AccessLevel.SYSTEM_MODE case, distinct from WITH USER_MODE code both queries and updates data on behalf of a user. Completing a milestone is the former -- the entitlement engines completion signal, not a field the agent deliberately edits. Granting Edit on CaseMilestone was rejected because it repeats the exact widen-the-persona anti-pattern skills/apex/test-class-standards Gotcha 15 already named in this build's own fixtures.
findings.recommendation: None -- recorded as the grounding for the choice the task required.

findings.title: Cross-skill tension: apex-stripinaccessible-and-fls-enforcement's trigger-body line is imprecise at 67.0+ for a class a trigger calls
findings.detail: That skill states a trigger body runs in system mode at every API version and that the 67.0 default-user-mode change does not reach it. Read literally and applied to this class, that would predict F-62 could not happen. It does not resolve the tension: CaseMilestoneService.completeMilestones is a method on a separate class, not code inside the literal trigger block, and skills/apex/apex-security-patterns (quoting the Apex Developer Guide) states the finer rule that trigger-body database operations run in user mode at 67.0+ unless system mode is explicitly named -- a default that reaches called classes too. skills/apex/entitlement-apex-hooks' own reference example predicts this exact failure by name. Per standards/source-hierarchy.md, the docs-grounded skill governs.
findings.recommendation: Flagged for build-doc-keeper to carry forward as a skill-authoring follow-up: apex-stripinaccessible-and-fls-enforcement's Before Starting line should distinguish the literal trigger block from classes a trigger calls, or cite the version-gated exception apex-security-patterns already documents.

process_observations.observation: The diagnosis handed down was independently confirmed against both the code and the org-facing permission-set source before any line was changed -- the grep for CaseMilestone across artefacts/M2-S02/ and the direct read of Case_Agent_Core's objectPermissions block both corroborate it exactly, with nothing to revise.

Four org-executed runs (F-59 through F-62) were needed to fully validate one test class, each exposing a defect the previous repair's fix uncovered rather than caused: persona context, then fixture-seeding scope, then process lookup, then object-level access. This is evidence of a genuinely layered set of independent defects converging, not any one repair being wrong, but it is also four rounds of compiles-and-appears-correct that a design-only build cannot itself catch.
